title: Man. Post. Cap. IX tip — sinned in Adam as we were in him: by natural generation, not divine imputation
pass_a_gloss: All sinned in Adam as they were in him. They were in him not by imputation of his being, but because his being causes the being of all. So they sinned in him not by imputation of his sin, but because his sin causes theirs—as his being causes ours—not by intervening divine imputation, but by natural generation and propagation.
pass_b_english: All men sinned in Adam as they were in him.
But they were in him not by imputation of his being (τοῦ εἶναι), but because his being is the cause of the being of all.

Therefore all sinned in him not by imputation of his sin, but because his sin is the cause of the sin of all—a cause, I say, in the same way his being is the cause of ours: not by intervening divine imputation, but through natural generation and propagation.
source_text: Peccavisse omnes homines in Adamo, quomodo in eo fuerunt. Fuerunt autem in eo non imputatione τοῦ εἶναι ipsius, sed quia eius esse est causa τοῦ εἶναι omnium. Peccavisse igitur in eo omnes, non peccati ipsius imputatione, sed quia peccatum eius est causa peccati omnium; causa, inquam, eo modo quo ipsius esse est causa nostri, non imputationis divinae interventu, sed per generationem & propagationem naturalem.

choices.choice: In Adam by being-cause via generation, not divine imputation
